identityReview: Matched Wang Tao / Frank Wang, DJI founder, with university biographies and award citation, corporate product statements and current Forbes profile. Distinct from similarly named academics, software founders and business figures. 1980 birth year directly supported by HKUST 2026 citation; citizenship China in Forbes. Full birthday and birthplace omitted.
lifeStatusEvidence: IT Home April 10, 2026 reports a LatePost interview published April 9 with comments on staff movement and organizational management. HKUST January 14 release identifies him as an inaugural January 10 award recipient. Forbes profile updated November 4, 2026 lists founder and chairman.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Opened HKUST 2014 education profile, 2019 award report, 2026 award citation PDF and award announcement; DJI original Phantom, Inspire 1 and Mavic Pro statements; current Forbes profile; IT Home report attributing interview to LatePost. Original LatePost interview not obtained.
sourceReview.scope: Identity, education, leadership, team product milestones, awards and 2026 interview activity.
corrections: HKUST records BEng 2006 and MPhil 2011. MPhil is a research master’s degree, not a doctorate. Generic Forbes BA/BS and MS labels are not used over university records. Undergraduate discipline wording varies in university pages, so main fact uses BEng without imposing a single expanded title.

HKUST 2026 citation directly gives birth year 1980 and identifies Li Zexiang as MPhil supervisor. No birthday inferred from current age. Growing up in Hangzhou does not prove birthplace, so no birthplace retained.
Company founding in 2006 supported by HKUST and Forbes. Dormitory origin and Shenzhen business development are not converted into an unverified exact incorporation day.
Phantom announcement dated January 7, 2013 describes pre-tuned Naza-M/GPS aircraft that can carry GoPro or other lightweight camera. Not described as having the later models’ built-in 4K camera.
Inspire 1 event occurred November 12, 2014 in San Francisco; company retrospective page is dated November 20. Timeline uses event date, not page date. World-first promotional claim omitted.

Mavic Pro statement header is September 28, 2016, but dateline explicitly September 27 and product-information page also dates launch September 27. Timeline uses launch date. Folding design and stabilized 4K camera are company specifications, not an independently tested performance benchmark.

2019 IEEE Robotics and Automation Award shared by Wang and Li Zexiang. University report says ICRA May 20–24 but does not specify award day; timeline conservatively retains year. Award image explicitly says Wang is not pictured, so it cannot serve as his portrait.

HKUST inaugural Distinguished Engineering Alumni Award ceremony January 10, 2026, reported January 14. Three recipients; Wang’s category is professional achievement and global impact. Not honorary doctorate. No assumption that being a recipient proves physical attendance.

April 9, 2026 is LatePost publication date as reported by IT Home April 10, not a confirmed interview-recording day. Management views are attributed and are not evidence that organizational problems have been resolved. No long quotation retained.

Current Forbes and April interview report call him founder and chairman. HKUST 2026 award materials call him founder and CEO. Profile uses supported chairman title without inventing a CEO transition date; 2014 CEO/CTO labels are historical.

Products are achievements of company engineering teams, not sole inventions by Wang. Mentor contributions retained. No unsupported current market-share, wealth, employee count or personal ownership percentage.

Searched current regulatory/ownership context and read DroneXL overview, but no legal findings asserted without original case records. No blanket safety, regulatory approval or military-use claim included.
sourceReview.limits: AI authored and reviewed; no human or native-language certification. No original LatePost full interview, independent product tests, market-share audit or comprehensive regulatory history.

portraitReview.rightsEvidence: Forbes portrait credits Visual China Group/Getty Images. DroneXL search snippet cited Capricorn4049/Commons CC BY-SA 4.0, but opened article caption credits DJI and gives no confirmed Commons source. Search snippet is insufficient proof of license. University photographs have no confirmed reusable license.
portraitReview.unresolved: No verified reusable portrait source established. Resolve source identity and rights before download and visual/crop/color checks. No new image download or visual inspection performed for this person. 2019 award photo explicitly excludes Wang.

translationReview.scope: All 32 Chinese fields and seven translations checked for mentor/team attribution, BEng/MPhil distinction, shared 2019 award, 2026 award ceremony versus report date, 2014/2016 event versus page dates, original Phantom camera capability and secondary interview attribution.
